summary:
Public Law 118-107, the "Congenital Heart Futures Reauthorization Act of 2024" (H.R. 7189, enacted November 21, 2024), amends section 399V-2 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 280g-13) to reauthorize and expand the national congenital heart disease research, surveillance, and awareness program administered by the Secretary of Health and Human Services.

Section 1 supplies the short title (codified as a note to 42 U.S.C. 201).

Section 2 effects three operative amendments to section 399V-2:

First, it redesignates existing subsections (f) and (g) as subsections (g) and (h), respectively, thereby making room for a new subsection (f).

Second, it inserts a new subsection (f) ("Report and Strategy"), which imposes two sequential deliverables on the Secretary. Paragraph (1) requires the Secretary, not later than two years after the date of enactment, to issue a report to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions describing (A) past and present HHS activities to increase public awareness and knowledge of congenital heart disease, including efforts addressing patients' lifelong needs; (B) an assessment of past and present HHS activities to increase provider education and training; and (C) the current U.S. workforce capacity of providers treating adult congenital heart disease patients. Paragraph (2) requires the Secretary, not later than one year after submitting that report, to develop and submit to Congress a strategy for improving public awareness and provider education and training, including findings and recommendations to address (i) public-awareness and research gaps related to patients' lifelong needs (long-term outcomes, quality of life, mental health, health care utilization); (ii) workforce shortages among providers treating adult congenital heart disease patients, potentially through enhanced fellowship or continuing-education programs; and (iii) interagency and cross-stakeholder collaboration and information dissemination. In developing the strategy, the Secretary must consult, as appropriate, with qualified stakeholder groups, including patient organizations, health care professionals, research entities, health insurance providers, accrediting organizations, and relevant Federal agencies (naming CDC, NIH, and HRSA).

Third, it amends the authorization-of-appropriations provision in the redesignated subsection (h) by striking "2020 through 2024" and inserting "2025 through 2029," extending the existing authorization of appropriations for an additional five fiscal years. This is an authorization only; the bill makes no appropriation.

The Act contains no separate effective-date provision; its amendments take effect upon enactment.
